transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess my eating has been kind of off. Some weeks I barely eat dinner, and then other nights I’m in the kitchen late, eating crackers or sweets after everyone’s gone to bed. It’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should come in.
When you eat late at night, do you feel unable to stop or control how much you’re eating?

Yeah… kind of. It’s not like a huge amount every time, but some nights I’m just standing there eating crackers or sweets and I don’t really stop until I feel embarrassed or tired. Other weeks I barely want dinner at all. It’s just been… all over the place.
When this happens, do you eat what most people would consider a large amount of food for that period of time?

I don’t think it’s always a huge amount. It’s more like… my eating is all over the place. Some weeks I barely touch dinner, and then other nights I’m standing in the kitchen eating crackers or sweets after everyone’s gone to bed.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?
No… I don’t make myself throw up.
During those late-night eating episodes, do you feel like you can’t stop eating once you’ve started?
Sometimes, yeah. Once I’m there eating crackers or sweets, I kind of just… keep going. Not always a lot, but it feels hard to stop in the moment.
After these eating episodes, do you do anything to try to undo the calories, like using laxatives?
No… I don’t use laxatives or anything like that. I just kind of feel bad about it and move on.
After you eat like that, do you ever do hard exercise on purpose to make up for it?
No… I don’t really do hard exercise to make up for it. I’m not… I’m not doing that.
When this happens, do you eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?
Sometimes it feels like a lot, yeah… like crackers and sweets, just standing there eating. I don’t know if it’s, um, “unusually large,” but it can feel more than I meant to.
Do these eating episodes usually happen after you’ve gone to sleep and then wake up again to eat?
Not usually after I’ve already fallen asleep, no. It’s more… after everyone’s gone to bed, I’m still up and I end up in the kitchen eating crackers or sweets.
After nights when you eat like that, do you deliberately skip meals or eat much less the next day to make up for it?

Sometimes I eat less the next day, but it’s not really planned to make up for it. My eating’s just been… all over the place. Some nights I’m eating crackers or sweets after everyone’s asleep, and other times I barely touch dinner.
During one of these episodes, do you eat an amount of food that most people would consider definitely larger than what they would eat in the same period?

I don’t know if most people would call it definitely larger. It’s more that my eating’s been all over the place… some weeks I barely touch dinner, and other nights I’m just standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone’s gone to bed.
Has there been any time when, during one of these episodes, you were sure you ate what most people would consider a very large amount of food?

I’m not sure I’d call it a very large amount. It’s more just… my eating is all over the place. Some nights I’m barely eating dinner, and other nights I’m in the kitchen late eating crackers or sweets after everyone’s gone to bed.
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress?

Yeah… somewhat. It’s embarrassing more than anything. The eating being so all over the place is part of what made me come in—some weeks I barely eat dinner, and then other nights I’m standing in the kitchen after everyone’s asleep eating crackers or sweets.
During these episodes, do you ever eat what you yourself would consider a clearly large amount of food?

Not clearly large, no… not like that. It’s more that it swings around. Some weeks I barely eat dinner, and then other nights I’m standing in the kitchen late eating crackers or sweets when everyone’s asleep.
How much does your body weight or shape affect how you feel about yourself?
I don’t know… I mean, I don’t like thinking about it much. It probably affects me some, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly focused on it.
Has your weight gotten to a level that a doctor told you was significantly low?

No, not that I know of. A doctor hasn’t told me it was significantly low. It’s more just… my eating has been really inconsistent—some weeks I barely eat dinner, other nights I’m up late eating crackers or sweets.
Has this late-night eating ever involved an amount of food that you were sure was objectively large?

I don’t think so… not objectively large. It’s more that my eating’s been really uneven—some weeks I barely eat dinner, and then some nights I’m just in the kitchen eating crackers or sweets after everyone’s gone to bed.
When you eat in the kitchen late at night, are you fully awake and aware of what you’re doing?
Yeah… I’m awake. I know what I’m doing. It’s just late, and I’m standing there eating crackers or sweets when everyone else is asleep. It’s not like I’m sleepwalking or anything.
Do you eat more than a quarter of your day’s food after your evening meal?
I’m not really sure it’s that much. Some nights I do eat after dinner—like crackers or sweets—but other weeks I’m barely eating dinner at all, so it’s hard for me to judge.
Do you usually have little or no appetite for breakfast in the morning?
I guess… some mornings, yeah, I don’t really feel like eating much. My eating’s just been kind of all over the place lately.
